title: Treat the landing (/, /en/) as a scroll-driven experience on purpose: do not strip Lenis, pins or held scenes to satisfy the old no-wheel/no-hijack rules
body: Author's direction (2026-10-26): the landing IS the experience, not a widget inside a page. One continuous scroll that ends in the CV download. A 'wow' effect outranks performance (performance is kept where possible). Scroll hijacking is ACCEPTED on the landing only, against the 2026-08-14 visual-system spec and CLAUDE.md invariant 7 (CLAUDE.md names the exception). So Lenis's wheel listener (src/scripts/v2/main.ts) and holdScroll/releaseScroll in util.ts are deliberate. Since 2026-10-29 the landing serves / and /en/ (src/components/v2/Landing.astro). When test:js or test:bundle fail on it, the fix is an explicit exception written into CLAUDE.md and the checks (scripts/pages-with-js.ts, the bundle budget), never deleting the behaviour and never a silent allowlist (docs/TODO.md stage 5). Also decided: no 3D node map, no three.js, no photo, video or 3D portrait; the ring-with-N logo and the dark tone are the anchors. The landing does not reuse the CV components: it builds from getView('portfolio'). /cv and /en/cv stay at zero JS. Positioning: a web developer who adapts to new technology, shown, not claimed. Tone: sells through subtlety.
not_derivable: CLAUDE.md's invariant and the v1 spec say the opposite (no wheel listeners, no hijacking), so an agent fixing the failing gates would remove the core of the landing.
